key_insight: A generalized mixing-plane formulation is introduced that conserves mass and remains thermodynamically consistent for compressible reacting-mixture turbomachinery flows.
engineering_relevance: It enables steady whole-engine simulations that couple compressor, combustor, and turbine while handling non-ideal post-combustor gas composition.
method: Uses a nested solve: outer pressure-root search plus inner enthalpy inversion.
Adds physical-state checks and power-law pressure sampling for robustness near low normal velocities.
Reduces to the classic mixing-plane method when mixture fraction goes to zero.
evidence_signal: Validated on a quasi-1D interface test, a transonic compressor case, and a KJ66 micro-turbojet whole-engine simulation, with maximum relative mass-flow error below 0.11% and good agreement with experiments.
watch_item: The approach adds thermodynamic inversion and root-finding complexity, so robustness and cost may be sensitive near the pressure upper bound or in very low-throughflow conditions.
paper_title: Generalised Mixing-Plane Method for Compressible Reacting-Mixture Flows in Steady Multiphysics Turbomachinery Simulations
